question: Let $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & i \\ -i & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ where $i^2 = -1$. Then $A^2$ equals:
explanation:
$A^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & i \\ -i & 0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & i \\ -i & 0 \end{pmatrix}$

First row:

$0 \times 0 + i \times -i = 0 + (-i^2) = 0 + 1 = 1$

$0 \times i + i \times 0 = 0$

Second row:

$-i \times 0 + 0 \times -i = 0$

$-i \times i + 0 \times 0 = -i^2 = 1$

So $A^2 = I$.
